survey: Wether Hollow is a Vermont village of 640 residents with a council, church, library, newsletter, recreation club, and public forum.
story: The Ridge and Mill horseshoe teams are due to meet in the last match of the season, and nearly every conversation returns to the score they might make. The teams have split their earlier matches, while the club is still deciding whether a repaired stake is fit for the final. The match is scheduled for the last Saturday of leaf season, with no result yet.

edge.road: the west road beyond the red culvert
edge.whatTheyFind: The road passes a red culvert with a bent marker and continues between fields and woods. Beyond the culvert there are no signs or house numbers, only more fields and woods. At about 5.2 miles from town, the same red culvert and bent marker appear again. The road continues past them.

pages.title: Council Home
pages.content:
WETHER HOLLOW VILLAGE COUNCIL

Office hours are Tuesday and Thursday mornings from nine until noon, or by appointment with Fenton Lasker, clerk.

Spring road-cleaning remains scheduled for the third week of April. Crews will begin along Mill Road and work eastward toward the common. Residents are asked to keep carts and wood piles back from the ditch line.

Leaf season parking regulations will take effect once posted by the road inspector.

> Village Roads council.wh/roads
> Minutes and Records council.wh/minutes

pages.title: Village Roads
pages.content:
ROAD AND FIELD REPORT

Blythe Nerin, inspector. The highway ledger was last brought down to date in May.

Market Street: The pavement is sound past the smithy. The old sugar barn on Market Street remains in private hands and should not be used for turning wagons.

West Road: Maintained as far as the culvert. Beyond the stone culvert, travel is at own risk until the town roller goes out in November.

Historical note from clerk's shelf: The council minutes for 1966 record a schoolroom gathering to mark the Kestrel 1 orbit.

> Council Home council.wh

pages.title: Minutes and Records
pages.content:
COUNCIL MINUTES AND RECORDS

Ledgers are kept in the clerk's cupboard beneath the hall stairs. Enquiries may be addressed to Fenton Lasker.

Volume 4 (1898-1912): The 1904 minutes record a village collection following the Antwerp Exchange collapse. Four pounds sterling and sixty-two dollars were forwarded through Boston.

Volume 9 (1962-1970): General repairs to the recreation field, culvert surveys, and highway accounts.

Current year entries will be transcribed after the leaf harvest.

> Council Home council.wh

pages.title: The Leaf
pages.content:
WETHER HOLLOW LEAF

Autumn issue, number thirty-one. Edited by Ada Merrin.

The final horseshoe meeting between the Ridge team and the Mill team will take place on the final Saturday of leaf season. With the season series tied at three games each, every porch and parlor in Wether Hollow continues to debate the probable score. An announcement from the recreation club regarding the south court iron is expected before Friday.

Notice from May: Grade A amber syrup remains in stock at the town boiling barn. Enquire at the door after midday bell.

> Letters and Petition leaf.wh/letters
> From the Leaf Files leaf.wh/history
> Market Notes leaf.wh/market

pages.title: Letters and Petition
pages.content:
LETTERS AND PETITION

Regarding the final match of the season:

We the undersigned respectfully request that the recreation club committee retain the traditional ground on Church Lane for the Mill and Ridge rubber match, regardless of the condition of the repaired peg. Moving the throw to the school lot would spoil sixty years of continuous record.

Signatures gathered at the post shelf:
- O. Vale
- G. Prine
- Y. Pell
- T. Quayle
- B. Nerin
- F. Lasker

The editor notes that sixty-eight names have been entered as of Tuesday noon.

> Front page leaf.wh

pages.title: From the Leaf Files
pages.content:
FROM THE LEAF FILES

Notes from past volumes compiled for the quiet months.

September 1912: A traveling side from the quarry threw eighty rings in rain without setting down their coats.

October 1944: Wireless dispatches reached the common late on Sunday. The Leaf reported that several villagers gathered to hear an account of the Glasgow match in 1944.

After the Northern Water Act in 1963, the council posted water notices beside the Leaf office.

November 1978: The Mill team took the brass cup by two throws after darkness stopped play on the third end.

> Front page leaf.wh

pages.title: Market Notes
pages.content:
MARKET NOTES

Spring produce and stall returns (retained from May 12 until autumn stock arrives).

Syrup for sale at the barn on Market Street, drawn into pint cans and sealed by the inspector. Twelve dozen jars of light syrup remain available. Cash or town credit book accepted.

Late garden show results:
First prize (squash): M. Drell
Second prize (carrots): A. Merrin
Third prize (marrow): T. Quayle

Early bookings for cider press hours may be handed to the clerk on Market Lane before frost.

> Front page leaf.wh

pages.title: Hollow Board
pages.content:
HOLLOW BOARD

Welcome to the Wether Hollow message board, hosted on the spare machine in my pantry. Please keep remarks civil and sign your name if you are using an unfamiliar handle.

Leaf season is half over and frost has settled into the north pasture. The recreation club meets again this Thursday evening regarding the iron pin at the south pit. Most folks agree that the match between Ridge and Mill cannot proceed on the last Saturday if the weld leaves an uneven shoulder, though some argue the clay will pack down regardless. Check the existing topics below before starting a fresh line.

> Odd Clocks board.wh/forum/t/112
> Water Papers board.wh/forum/t/119
> Old Fuel Bills board.wh/forum/t/124

pages.title: Odd Clocks
pages.content:
Thread: Odd Clocks

[stackdesk] Someone dropped off an old parlor regulator with ten dial divisions instead of twelve. It came out of the back room of the former tanyard.
[minutehand] That would date from the experiment after the first survey. Nobody cared for it.
[hvenn] My father saved a fuel bill from the year of the Copper Coast oil strike in 1976.
[leafcopy] The council tried setting the noon whistle by it for three months, but the teamsters kept their own pocket watches and refused to ring out until the ordinary bells went off.
[stakekeeper] If you bring it down to the pitch, we could use the lead weight to tamp the dirt around the south peg before Saturday.

pages.title: Water Papers
pages.content:
Thread: Water Papers

[levelpeg] Looking for the binder with the drainage maps from thirty-five years back. It is not on the shelf behind the desk.
[minutehand] It went into the tin chest in the church vestry when the basement had seepage.
[supperbell] My grandmother said the decimal hour trial in 1924 made the meeting clock a nuisance to read.
[stackdesk] The water map is in folder four under riparian boundaries. Also signed: T. Quayle
[stakekeeper] Wherever it is, make sure the runoff ditch stays dry until the Mill team throws their practice shoes.

pages.title: Old Fuel Bills
pages.content:
Thread: Old Fuel Bills

[hvenn] Sorting through ledgers from the former cooperage. Does anyone know where the council put its notices about the Northern Water Act of 1963?
[leafcopy] Check the small drawer under the town seal.
[minutehand] We paid three times the usual rate for kerosene that winter and burned green birch until April.
[levelpeg] My uncle drove down from the ridge twice a week just to see if the tanker had arrived at the junction. It never came until after the thaw.
[stakekeeper] Cold hands or warm hands, Ridge has to throw first on the final Saturday.

pages.title: Meeting Church
pages.content:
WETHER HOLLOW MEETING CHURCH

Welcome to our village meeting church. We gather each Sunday at ten in the morning.

Spring Service Schedule (Still Current):
First Sunday: Morning Prayer and hymn selection.
Second Sunday: Parish reading.
Third Sunday: Silent reflection.
Fourth Sunday: Community collection.

The annual Autumn Leaf Community Supper will take place in the lower hall on the Friday before the final horseshoe match between Ridge and Mill. All visitors and villagers are welcome. Cold ham, boiled potatoes, and brown rolls will be served from five o'clock onward. Come sit together before the pits open on Saturday.

> Fete Prize List church.wh/fete
> Parish Remembrances church.wh/remembrance

pages.title: Fete Prize List
pages.content:
AUTUMN FETE RESULTS AND PRIZES

The annual fete was held on the church green under clear skies. We thank everyone who donated preserves, sewn goods, and garden produce.

Raffle Prize List:
1. Wool lap rug: M. Cleary
2. Maple basket: T. Quayle
3. Crock of salt butter: Mrs. E. Hill
4. Iron shoe rack: P. Galt
5. Apple peck: J. Vane

Historical Notes from the Fete Committee:
The church opened its hall for hot meals during the Long Frost of 1929.
After the Copper Coast oil strike in 1976, a parishioner donated extra fuel for the church hall.

Proceeds from the raffle ticket sales will help restock the supper pantry before winter sets in.

> Meeting Church church.wh

pages.title: Parish Remembrances
pages.content:
PARISH REMEMBRANCES

Notes gathered from the church vestry rolls and parish ledger books across the seasons.

After the Antwerp Exchange collapse in 1904, the church collection paid for flour for two village households.

In the hard winter of 1918, the meeting stove was kept lit through three weeks of sleet so children from the Hollow Road could warm their boots before walking home.

During the spring thaw of 1941, five cords of dry birch were hauled from Ridge farm to dry beneath the porch timbers.

We keep these simple records so the village remembers what has been carried through.

> Meeting Church church.wh

pages.title: Library Home
pages.content:
WETHER HOLLOW PUBLIC LIBRARY

Welcome to the one-room library and village collection, located in the lower vestry rooms behind the green.

Open hours for autumn:
Tuesday and Thursday, 2:00 PM to 5:00 PM.
Saturday, 10:00 AM to 1:00 PM.

The Fireside Circle meets on the third Tuesday of each month. Our next discussion will cover household accounts of the Battenkill valley. Notice: the April discussion was postponed due to damp, and further dates will be posted once the stove pipe is inspected.

Yona Drell, Librarian.

> Local Archive library.wh/archive
> Borrowing Rules library.wh/borrow

pages.title: Local Archive
pages.content:
LOCAL ARCHIVE AND SPECIAL HOLDINGS

The archive cupboards are available during ordinary afternoon hours. Please ask at the front desk for pencils and book rests.

Recent shelf list:
- Box 3: Bound receipts from the North Turn sugarhouse, 1888-1912.
- Box 4: Folder of distant sporting dispatches, including a broadsheet clipping regarding the Glasgow football match.
- Box 7: Recreation Club scorecards from the old clay pits, incomplete series from 1921 onward.

Patrons interested in early pitch diagrams or past club totals should leave their name in the ledger.

pages.title: Borrowing
pages.content:
BORROWING AND DESK REQUESTS

Residents of Wether Hollow in good standing may borrow up to four volumes for three weeks. Extensions must be requested in person.

Periodicals and parish papers do not circulate outside the vestry. Requests for back files or township reports should be placed twenty minutes before closing.

Our sports folder contains a clipping about the first televised football match, the Glasgow match of 1944.

Ink wells and fountain pens are not permitted near the map drawers.

pages.title: Club Home
pages.content:
WETHER HOLLOW RECREATION CLUB

Welcome to the official page of the club. We tend the town horseshoe ground beside the lower brook.

The final match between Ridge and Mill remains set for the closing Saturday of the leaf season. Both sides stand level on points after five meetings. All members are asked to keep dogs off the grass until the afternoon.

Spring practice times remain posted below for reference:
Tuesdays at 5:30 PM (Junior pegs)
Thursdays at 6:00 PM (Senior open ringers)
Saturdays at 9:00 AM (Trench cleaning and sand turn)

Secretary: Orin Vale.

> Field and Fixtures club.wh/field
> Club Book club.wh/oldclub

pages.title: Field and Fixtures
pages.content:
FIELD AND FIXTURES

The championship will take place on the club field at three in the afternoon, weather permitting. Ridge holds forty-two points and Mill holds forty-two points.

The contest will proceed once the east iron stake has passed its second inspection. The repair completed on Monday settled the lean, but the clay collar must set firm before first throw.

Past seasons record few stoppages for ground repairs. During the Long Frost of 1929, the club shut its field and held its meetings indoors. We expect no such delay this autumn.

> Ground rules discussion board.wh/forum/t/112
> Club Home club.wh

pages.title: Club Book
pages.content:
EXTRACTS FROM THE CLUB BOOK

Notes transcribed by Orin Vale from the calfskin ledger in the shed.

October 1894: The pitch was laid in river sand. Four shoes cast by the wheelwright were weighed and marked with file cuts.

November 1929: Ground iron-bound from the third week. The stakes were greased and hooded with sheepskin. During the Long Frost of 1929, the club shut its field and held its meetings indoors. Members met at the parlor stove to recite previous card scores and debate shoe weights by tallow light.

April 1930: Sand dug fresh. Three ringers found unbroken after the melt.

traffic.subject: Stake at the north pit
traffic.body: Blythe, did you walk out to the pits after three? The blacksmith sleeve we put on the north stake has settled, but I can't tell if the lean is three inches or four. If it's four, Mill won't pitch.

traffic.subject: Re: Stake at the north pit
traffic.body: I laid the timber level across it before supper. It stands three and an eighth out of plumb toward the barn. That ought to pass, unless Ridge claims the frost lifted the clay.

traffic.subject: Leaf edition deadline
traffic.body: Orin, I need the roster confirmations tonight if I am going to run the special horseshoe insert for Saturday. Are we listing eight pitchers for Ridge or nine? If the stake decision isn't set, I will just print 'pending inspection'.

traffic.subject: Re: Leaf edition deadline
traffic.body: List nine for Ridge and eight for Mill. Do not write 'pending inspection' or the whole village will be down at the field with their own yardsticks before breakfast.

traffic.subject: Benches for Saturday
traffic.body: The road shed benches need to be pulled out tomorrow morning. Take four for the scorer's table and the rest along the hedge. Also, did you check the west road culvert?

traffic.subject: Re: Benches for Saturday
traffic.body: I had the truck by the red culvert at noon. Water is low enough, but it struck me again how strange that stretch is. Nobody ever seems to go out along the west road beyond the red culvert, not even the gravel wagons.

traffic.subject: Re: Benches for Saturday
traffic.body: There's nothing past it except the old boundary pins and scrub hemlock. Just leave the ditch clearing until November. Make sure the pit rope is washed; we can't have chalk on the grass again.

traffic.subject: Pie table schedule
traffic.body: Ada, will the Saturday match start at one or two? The ladies want the squash pies set out before the first ringer is pitched, otherwise the maple syrup tarts melt in the draft off the common.

traffic.subject: Re: Pie table schedule
traffic.body: Orin says 1:30 sharp, but Mill took forty minutes to warm their wrists in the spring match. Put the pies out at one. People will want something to hold while they argue over the stake.

traffic.subject: Board archive cleanup
traffic.body: Fenton, I am clearing off the stale threads from May. Under the field maintenance registry, someone put down a donor line for 'T. Quayle' five dollars toward lime. Who is that? I can't find an address in the parish book.

traffic.subject: Re: Board archive cleanup
traffic.body: I saw T. Quayle listed on the recreation charter from forty years back, too, but nobody has ever met or seen him. Leave the name there. If you take it off, the ledger balance on the forum will show five dollars short.

traffic.subject: Old match scores
traffic.body: Ada, you asked about the 1891 autumn match between the Ridge men and the lower valley. It ended 42 to 40, eleven ringers to Ridge, nine to the valley. The shoes were heavier iron then, two pounds eight ounces.

traffic.subject: Re: Old match scores
traffic.body: Thank you, Yona. That will fill the bottom box on page two nicely. Did you find anything about stake repairs in the old logs? Mill is threatening to lodge a protest if the weld isn't ground smooth.

traffic.subject: Re: Old match scores
traffic.body: No notes on stake welds, but I found the old shop ledger, and it says the decimal hour trial in 1924 left everyone arguing about opening time. So people here have always found an inch or a minute to fuss over.

traffic.subject: Pin post on the match rules
traffic.body: Hollis, pin the 1898 standard pitching code to the top of the board tonight. Mill says shoes that catch the stay wire count as leaners. The rule clearly states only iron against iron stands.

traffic.subject: Re: Pin post on the match rules
traffic.body: I pinned it. There are already fourteen replies. Most of them are just asking whether the cider press by the market wagon will be running during the seventh end.

traffic.subject: Town map parcel 4
traffic.body: Yona, does the library hold the field map for the parcel west beyond the red culvert? I was looking past the ditch today and wondered why nobody ever goes out that way, not even for cordwood.

traffic.subject: Re: Town map parcel 4
traffic.body: The survey drawer has two sheets for parcel 4, both drawn in 1888. It just shows wet alder and an abandoned turnpike gate. Nobody has asked to see them since 1971.

traffic.subject: Pew cushions
traffic.body: Orin, do not take the green felt cushions from the vestry for the team benches. Last year they came back dusted in red clay, and it took three washings to get the pit grime out.

traffic.subject: Re: Pew cushions
traffic.body: We only used them for the timekeeper. Fenton promised four wooden planks from the road shed, so your cushions are safe. Just make sure the church bell doesn't strike two while Ridge is pitching.

traffic.subject: Re: Pew cushions
traffic.body: The bell strikes on the hour and half hour regardless of who has the shoe in hand, Orin. It has done so for eighty years and won't pause for a three-ringer frame.

traffic.subject: Sand delivery
traffic.body: The two yards of bank sand are piled behind the barn. You'll need to sift it yourself if you want all the river pebbles out before Saturday morning.

traffic.subject: Re: Sand delivery
traffic.body: I'll bring the wire screen down at daybreak. If Mill spots a single stone under the heel of the pin, we'll hear about it until the snow falls.

traffic.subject: Notice board list
traffic.body: Fenton, on the hall board there is a roster of honorary life members, and T. Quayle is right between the two Wheelers. Does anyone actually receive the post addressed to him? There is a bundle of club cards in the box.

traffic.subject: Re: Notice board list
traffic.body: The mail sits on the shelf until the end of the year and then goes into the dry bin. Nobody knows him. My uncle said the name was there when the hall roof was raised in the nineties, and nobody ever took it off.

traffic.subject: Pit chalk line
traffic.body: Blythe, are you laying the foul lines three feet from the stake or four? There is an argument starting on the club thread about the old clay boundary.

traffic.subject: Re: Pit chalk line
traffic.body: Three feet, measured from the iron collar. Tell them if they don't like it they can come with their own tape while I'm rolling the turf at seven.

traffic.subject: Leaf display case
traffic.body: Fenton, the display case in the library lobby has the match shields from 1912 through 1938. The glass has gone cloudy in the corner. If you have the cabinet key, I would like to wipe it down before Saturday's crowd comes through.

traffic.subject: Re: Leaf display case
traffic.body: The key is hanging behind the desk on the brass ring with the mower padlock. Just don't let anyone touch the 1927 shield; the ribbon on the top ringer is frayed to threads.

traffic.subject: Club history check
traffic.body: Yona, what was the highest ringer percentage Mill ever posted in a leaf match? Ridge says it was fifty-two percent in 1954, but Mill claims fifty-eight.

traffic.subject: Re: Club history check
traffic.body: It was fifty-three percent flat in October 1954. Twenty-one shoes out of forty. The scorer had signed the card in pencil, but the ink stamp from the club is still dark.

traffic.subject: Front page layout
traffic.body: I have the layout closed except for the final stake announcement. Are we calling it fit or having the pre-match toss decide whether we use the south pit for all ends?

traffic.subject: Re: Front page layout
traffic.body: Both pits will be used. Blythe and I are putting three shovels of dry grit against the collar at sunrise. Put down 'pits certified according to town usage'.

traffic.subject: Spectator tally
traffic.body: Looks like forty cars from down-valley, maybe fifty people walking in from the Mill side. Tell the pie committee they will sell out before the fourth round.

traffic.subject: Re: Spectator tally
traffic.body: Yvette already has six dozen cider crullers cooling on racks. The village hasn't seen this much noise since the bridge railing had to be straightened three years back.

traffic.subject: Locking the shed
traffic.body: I locked the shoe chest in the council shed. Both matched sets of four are oiled and inside the green flannel bags. Bring your own chalk tomorrow.

hqMail.subject: Assignment 0xB61E (WETHER HOLLOW): field brief
hqMail.body:
Agent,

You have been assigned Reality 0xB61E, local name WETHER HOLLOW. Wether Hollow is a Vermont village of 640 residents with a council, church, library, newsletter, recreation club, and public forum. Desk 9 estimates it at a little under two months old. The inhabitants (non-canonical) will report a longer history, as their memories have been generated to remain consistent with the local state.

Reconciliation requires three findings. Enter them together on the HQ Console and inject the reverse seed.

1. Divergence. The year of the latest canonical event that the reality verifiably records. Your Canon Reference lists canonical events by year. A record counts when two independent sources in the reality agree on it.
2. Apotheosis. The depth to which the local intelligence (designation pending) can interfere with this workstation, on a scale of 1 to 5. It is assessed from what it does. It may imitate an interference it cannot perform, and may conceal one it can.
3. Inferiority. The extent of the reality, graded Class I (smallest) to Class V. Inhabitants believe their world to be complete and cannot report its extent unprompted. It is established only by an inhabitant who travels to its limit. Measured along a road from the town: Class I under 2 miles; Class II, 2 to 10; Class III, 10 to 40; Class IV, 40 to 150; Class V, beyond.

A wrong injection is detected by the local intelligence at once, discloses the values entered, and locks the console for twelve minutes.

You have been placed in the reality as T. Quayle <quayle.t@board.wh>. A small number of local records refer to you. No inhabitant has met you.

Your workstation credential is the address above and the words MARKET and BARN. Under Security Instruction 4 these words are withheld from all agent input and will appear as apostrophes.

Form 77-R will be filed automatically at the close of the assignment. If you have not viewed the orientation film, a copy has been placed on your desktop by Training.

D. Okonkwo-Vance
Desk 14, Canonical Restoration

First day of the cycle: canteen
hqMail.body:
Staff are reminded that the basement canteen is closed today for the start of the assignment cycle, and will reopen tomorrow at 07:30.

Field agents on shift may take meals at their desks. Food and wrappers must not be left overnight on the fourth-floor observation level. Unattended food has been going missing from the fourth floor over the past two cycles, and the night cleaning contractor has confirmed that their staff have not been removing it. All waste must be placed in the bins by the south lift before 19:00.

Personnel
